data.why: The repo ships a ready-made session JSON (the only file type the app actually uploads) plus the real instrument CSVs the README walks through for manual sidebar entry and comparison; no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Fit per-peak LSS retention parameters (log10 k0, S) from two gradient scouting runs and check the quality of fit
Predict retention times, peak widths and resolution for a new candidate gradient programme before running it on the instrument
Compare predicted retention times against a real measured run to judge whether the model is trustworthy for this method
Explore how changing the candidate gradient's duration, start/end composition or segments shifts resolution and run time
Identify which peaks are being extrapolated outside the two scouting runs' calibrated composition window and how that should discount the predicted resolution
Save and reload a session file to keep inputs for a method under development

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately: fit two-run LSS parameters, predict tR/W½/Rs for any candidate programme, and grade how far each prediction extrapolates. Its phases follow the README, and all ten screens I opened back up their nodes. It needs small fixes before filing: add the held-out-run comparison as a task done outside the app, fix the order of tasks in the predict phase, use the term dwell volume instead of 'instrument offset', and add the dead-time plausibility feature.
